verdicts.summary: I could not break the detached, deduplicated status fetch. The waiter's 5s limit, the failure cooldown and the cache TTL fit together, and a waiter timeout or cancellation does not kill the fetch.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1279-1280 (the cooldown gate returns early only while now < retryAt; recordStatusRemoteRefreshFailure at 1520-1536 sets retryAt from the same cooldown(count) that the cache TTL uses at 1551-1556)

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1049-1066 (the 5 min timeout becomes a 'Git command timed out.' GitCommandError, not an interrupt, so a timed-out fetch is recorded as a failure and Fiber.join does not propagate an interrupt to the waiter)

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1517-1557 (a cooldown-gated or timed-out waiter returns success and is cached for 15s; the next poll re-enters the gate or joins the pending fiber, so there is no storm)

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1281-1322 (the fetch is forked into serviceScope and the pending fiber is deduplicated by statusFetches under Effect.uninterruptible; the waiter only does timeoutOption(5s) on Fiber.join)

apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1080-1082 (the fetch's 5 min timeout exceeds DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, so it skips gitProcesses and is bounded only by statusFetchProcesses(4); this is a benign change)
node_modules is absent from the checkout, so I could not open the effect forkIn or ChildProcess forceKillAfter source; I relied on the code and tests in the diff for those semantics

verdicts.summary: The pull waits only for a status fetch that is already in flight when the pull starts. A status poll that starts a fetch during the pull's own fetch can still collide on the upstream tracking-ref lock. The retry only narrows the refspec, so it fails again on the same ref and the user sees 'could not update a local reference'. The claim that the pull avoids colliding with the background fetch holds only for the in-flight case.
verdicts.scenario: 1. The user has no status fetch in flight, so statusFetches.get at 2667 is undefined and the pull proceeds without waiting. 2. `git pull --ff-only` starts and fetches origin, which takes seconds. 3. During that time the UI's status poll (statusDetailsRemote) misses its cache, because the 15s success TTL expired, and starts a background `git fetch origin`. Nothing in pullCurrentBranch blocks this: statusFetches is read once at 2667 and never registered or held during the pull. 4. Both fetches try to lock refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, and one reports 'cannot lock ref'. 5. If the pull's fetch loses, the retry at 2722 fetches only the upstream ref and can lose to the same background fetch on the same ref. The pull then fails at 2733-2736 with the lock detail.
verdicts.consequence: A pull intermittently fails with 'Git could not update a local reference' when the UI polls status during the pull. The user has to click Pull again. The window is small, so the effect is limited.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2664-2671 (statusFetches is read once, before the pull, and is never held during the pull)
apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2693-2741 (the retry covers only the unrelated-lock case and then throws the lock detail)
apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1278-1322 (nothing gates a new status fetch while a pull is running)
apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1236-1255 (the poll's remote name comes from @{upstream}, while the pull reads branch.<ref>.remote; both give the same remote for normal configs)
The unbounded Fiber.await at 2670 is already finding 0 and is not repeated here. I did not verify how often the client polls during a pull.
